Package com.acxiom.emailaudit.ingestion

Class ArchiveManager

java.lang.Object
com.acxiom.emailaudit.ingestion.ArchiveManager
public final class ArchiveManager extends Object
Moves processed HTML files into one of two archive sub-directories after the audit pipeline has finished evaluating them.

Archive layout

  <archive.root>/
    success/          ← files that completed without a fatal error
    failed/           ← files that could not be fully processed

Name-collision strategy

When a file with the same name already exists in the target directory a timestamp suffix is appended before the extension: report.html → report_20240601T103045123Z.html. The timestamp has millisecond precision, making collisions astronomically unlikely even under parallel execution.

Thread safety

  • Per-target-path ReentrantLocks (held in a ConcurrentHashMap) ensure that two threads racing to archive files with the same name do not both resolve to the same collision-free name and overwrite each other.
  • Directory creation is idempotent and guarded with Files.createDirectories(java.nio.file.Path, java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute<?>...).
  • File moves use ATOMIC_MOVE where the OS supports it, falling back to a non-atomic copy-then-delete otherwise.

Configuration keys

archive.root.dir Root directory for both sub-folders (default: target/audit-archive)
archive.success.dir Override for the success sub-directory name (default: success)
archive.failed.dir Override for the failed sub-directory name (default: failed)
